source_evidence.anchor: opening matrix setting and column notation
source_evidence.observation: The paper fixes A ∈ R^{m×n} with m ≥ n and rank(A)=n, writes A=(a₁,…,aₙ), Q=(q₁,…,qₙ), and R=(rⱼₖ), and describes the exact-arithmetic factorization A=QR with QᵀQ=Iₙ and nonsingular upper-triangular R.
Algorithm 2 (CGS-P) initializes r₁₁=||a₁||₂, q₁=a₁/r₁₁, R₁=(r₁₁), and Q₁=(q₁), before its loop k=2,…,n.

The paper assumes IEEE floating-point arithmetic and states fl(x+y)=(x+y)(1+δ), |δ|≤ε_M, for results in the normalized range. It adopts (1+ε_M)^{p(n)}=1+p(n)ε_M+O(ε_M²) for modest p(n), treating O(ε_M²) as making no significant contribution.

The paper defines A_k as the first k columns of A, κ₂(R_k)=||R_k||₂||R_k⁻¹||₂, c₁(m,1)=1, and c₄=c₂+2c₁. Theorem 1 assumes c₄(m,k)ε_Mκ₂(R_k)²<1 for each k for the R computed by Algorithm 2, and states, for k=1,…,n and to within O(ε_M²), Q_kR_k−A_k=ΔA_k with ||ΔA_k||₂≤c₁(m,k)||A_k||₂ε_M.
In the proof of Lemma 2, the authors use condition (3) to conclude that R is nonsingular and hence that rₖₖ>0 for every k.

source_evidence.anchor: Proof of Theorem 1, k=1 normalization-error display
source_evidence.observation: For the base case k=1, the proof repeats r₁₁=||a₁||₂(1+δ₁), with |δ₁|≤(0.5m+1)ε_M+O(ε_M²), so r₁₁ denotes a computed norm rather than an exact norm value.
The proof states that standard error bounds give q₁=(I+G₁)a₁/r₁₁ with ||G₁||₂≤ε_M.

source_evidence.anchor: exact residual identity immediately preceding equation (16)
source_evidence.observation: The proof then gives the exact algebraic identity A₁−Q₁R₁=a₁−q₁r₁₁=−G₁a₁.

binders: m and n are matrix dimensions with m≥n, and A∈R^{m×n} has rank(A)=n and columns a₁,…,aₙ; the use of a first column makes n≥1 implicit rather than separately stated. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 300, anchor: opening matrix setting and column notation]

ε_M is the machine unit, and Q,R are the floating-point matrices computed by Algorithm 2; A₁=(a₁), Q₁=(q₁), and R₁=(r₁₁) are their first-column/leading-block objects. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: Algorithm 2 first-column initialization; PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: definitions (2)]

The logical reading is: for each admissible input and computed output satisfying the inherited assumptions, there is a dimension-compatible G₁, depending on the computed first-column normalization, for which the displayed relation and bound hold. The existential quantifier is inferred from the phrase 'we can conclude from standard error bounds that,' because no explicit quantifier or shape declaration for G₁ is printed. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: standard-error-bound display preceding equation (16)]
hypotheses: A is in the paper's standing rectangular full-column-rank setting: A∈R^{m×n}, m≥n, rank(A)=n. This is inherited from the opening setup and is not restated in Theorem 1. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 300, anchor: opening matrix setting and column notation; PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: Theorem 1]

Q and R are the computed outputs of Algorithm 2 (CGS-P) in floating-point arithmetic with machine unit ε_M. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: Algorithm 2 and following floating-point model; PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: Theorem 1 condition (3)]
For every leading index k=1,…,n, the inherited conditioning restriction is c₄(m,k)ε_Mκ₂(R_k)²<1, where κ₂(R_k)=||R_k||₂||R_k⁻¹||₂. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: Theorem 1 condition (3)]

The displayed IEEE relative-error rule is asserted only for results in the normalized range, and the paper works to first order by treating O(ε_M²) terms as insignificant. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: floating-point model immediately following Algorithm 2]
conclusions: There exists a compatible error operator G₁ such that q₁=(I+G₁)a₁/r₁₁ and ||G₁||₂≤ε_M. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: standard-error-bound display preceding equation (16)]
The first-column residual satisfies the exact identity A₁−Q₁R₁=a₁−q₁r₁₁=−G₁a₁. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: exact residual identity immediately preceding equation (16)]

The complete bound is ||A₁−Q₁R₁||₂=||a₁−q₁r₁₁||₂≤||G₁||₂||a₁||₂≤ε_M||a₁||₂. No factor depending on m or n appears in this k=1 residual bound. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: equation (16), complete norm chain]

Equivalently, with the sign convention of Theorem 1 equation (4), Q₁R₁−A₁=G₁a₁ can be taken as ΔA₁ and obeys ||ΔA₁||₂≤c₁(m,1)||A₁||₂ε_M because c₁(m,1)=1 and a one-column matrix A₁ has the same 2-norm as a₁. This equivalence is inferred by negating the exact residual identity and matching it to (4). [PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: definitions (2) and conclusion (4); PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: exact residual identity and equation (16)]
definitions_and_conventions: A_k is the matrix formed by the first k columns of A; hence A₁ is the one-column matrix (a₁). Q_k and R_k are the corresponding recursively constructed leading factors, with Q₁=(q₁) and R₁=(r₁₁). [PDF p. 2, printed p. 300, anchor: column notation and Algorithm 1 block notation; PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: Algorithm 2 first-column initialization; PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: definition of A_k]

Although Algorithm 2's pseudocode writes r₁₁=||a₁||₂, the proof treats r₁₁ as the computed value r₁₁=||a₁||₂(1+δ₁), not as exact equality to the mathematical norm. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: Algorithm 2 first-column initialization; PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: k=1 normalization-error display]

I in q₁=(I+G₁)a₁/r₁₁ is the identity compatible with a₁; its size I_m is inferred from the multiplication, not explicitly subscripted. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 300, anchor: A∈R^{m×n} and a₁ column notation; PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: standard-error-bound display]

The theorem defines its perturbation with sign Q_kR_k−A_k=ΔA_k, while the proof of the base case displays A₁−Q₁R₁; the two are negatives and have equal 2-norms. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: conclusion (4); PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: exact residual identity and equation (16)]
implicit_context: Equation (16) is the k=1 induction base for Theorem 1 conclusion (4), not a standalone claim about arbitrary q₁ and r₁₁. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: opening of Proof of Theorem 1 and sentence following equation (16); PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: conclusion (4)]

The full-rank matrix setting is standing context from the introduction; Theorem 1 begins directly with the floating-point and conditioning assumptions. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 300, anchor: opening matrix setting; PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: Theorem 1]

Condition (3) is used in the appendix to obtain nonsingularity and rₖₖ>0 for all k, so in particular the computed denominator r₁₁ is positive. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 307, anchor: nonsingularity paragraph after equations (14)-(15)]

Theorem 1 is globally stated 'to within terms of O(ε_M²)'; the particular G₁ bound, residual identity, and equation (16) are nevertheless printed without an added O(ε_M²) remainder. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: Theorem 1 preamble to conclusions (4)-(8); PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: standard-error-bound display, exact residual identity, and equation (16)]
statement.algorithm_linkage: The selected claim is attached to the k=1 step of Algorithm 2 (CGS-P): compute r₁₁ from ||a₁||₂, divide to obtain q₁, and set R₁=(r₁₁), Q₁=(q₁). The k≥2 Pythagorean diagonal formula distinguishing CGS-P from CGS-S does not enter equation (16); the first-column initialization is also printed for Algorithm 1, but the enclosing theorem and proof explicitly concern Algorithm 2. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 300, anchor: Algorithm 1 initialization; PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: Algorithm 2 initialization; PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: Theorem 1; PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: k=1 proof and equation (16)]
numerical_model: The paper assumes IEEE floating-point arithmetic with machine unit ε_M and explicitly gives fl(x+y)=(x+y)(1+δ), |δ|≤ε_M, for normalized-range results. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: floating-point model immediately following Algorithm 2]

It adopts the first-order convention (1+ε_M)^{p(n)}=1+p(n)ε_M+O(ε_M²) for modest p(n), with O(ε_M²) treated as insignificant. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: linear approximation following the IEEE model]
For the computed norm, r₁₁=||a₁||₂(1+δ₁) with |δ₁|≤(0.5m+1)ε_M+O(ε_M²). [PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: k=1 normalization-error display]

For the computed division/normalization, the source invokes unspecified 'standard error bounds' to assert q₁=(I+G₁)a₁/r₁₁ and ||G₁||₂≤ε_M. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: standard-error-bound display preceding equation (16)]
error_notions: The selected error is the normwise first-column factorization residual A₁−Q₁R₁ (equivalently the perturbation Q₁R₁−A₁ in Theorem 1's sign convention), measured against the input scale ||a₁||₂=||A₁||₂. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: conclusion (4); PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: exact residual identity and equation (16)]

G₁ models error in the computed normalization q₁ and is controlled only through the matrix 2-norm bound ||G₁||₂≤ε_M in the printed passage. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: standard-error-bound display]

The residual identity is exact algebra in the displayed computed quantities once the G₁ representation is accepted; the final inequality is a forward bound on that residual and simultaneously supplies the k=1 normwise backward perturbation ΔA₁. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: conclusion (4); PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: exact residual identity and equation (16)]
norms: Every selected bound uses ||·||₂. The conventional reading is the Euclidean 2-norm for vectors and the induced spectral 2-norm for matrices, but the cited pages do not explicitly define those norm constructions. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 300, anchor: Algorithm 1 norm notation; PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: κ₂ definition; PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: equation (16)]
Equation (16) directly identifies the 2-norm of the m×1 matrix residual A₁−Q₁R₁ with the 2-norm of the vector residual a₁−q₁r₁₁. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: equation (16), first equality]

The step ||a₁−q₁r₁₁||₂≤||G₁||₂||a₁||₂ uses the operator-vector submultiplicative 2-norm inequality together with the preceding exact identity. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: exact residual identity and equation (16)]
constants_and_indexing: The selected case is exactly k=1; Algorithm 2's loop and Pythagorean formula begin at k=2. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: Algorithm 2 initialization and loop]

The theorem's residual constant is c₁(m,1)=1, and equation (16) realizes that k=1 coefficient. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: definition (2) and conclusion (4); PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: equation (16)]

The norm-computation perturbation uses the separate coefficient 0.5m+1 in |δ₁|≤(0.5m+1)ε_M+O(ε_M²); that m-dependent coefficient does not appear in equation (16). [PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: k=1 normalization-error display and equation (16)]

Condition (3) is indexed over every leading block k and uses c₄(m,k)ε_Mκ₂(R_k)²<1; it is inherited by the k=1 proof even though it does not occur in the final display (16). [PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: condition (3); PDF p. 9, printed p. 307, anchor: nonsingularity consequence]
higher_order_terms: The paper's general convention discards or neglects contributions O(ε_M²) under a linear approximation for modest p(n). [PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: linear approximation following the IEEE model]

The G₁ bound, exact residual identity, and equation (16) contain no printed O(ε_M²) remainder; adding such a term to equation (16) would not reproduce the displayed passage exactly. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: standard-error-bound display, exact residual identity, and equation (16)]
exceptional_values: The explicit relative-error formula is restricted to results in the normalized range. The selected pages provide no model for subnormal results, underflow, overflow, infinities, or NaNs. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: floating-point model immediately following Algorithm 2]

The inherited full-column-rank setting excludes a₁=0 in exact arithmetic, and condition (3) is used to conclude r₁₁>0, so the division defining q₁ has a nonzero computed denominator within the theorem's regime. undebatable_constraints: The input is in the standing real rectangular setting A∈R^{m×n}, m≥n, rank(A)=n, with a first column a₁. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 300, anchor: opening matrix setting and column notation]
The claim concerns computed Q,R from Algorithm 2 under Theorem 1's all-leading-block condition c₄(m,k)ε_Mκ₂(R_k)²<1. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: Theorem 1 condition (3)]

The first computed objects are r₁₁, q₁, R₁=(r₁₁), and Q₁=(q₁); the selected result is indexed at k=1. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: Algorithm 2 first-column initialization; PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: k=1 proof]
The inherited condition is used to make every computed diagonal positive, including r₁₁>0. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 307, anchor: nonsingularity paragraph after equations (14)-(15)]
The paper asserts q₁=(I+G₁)a₁/r₁₁ together with ||G₁||₂≤ε_M; neither part may be omitted. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: standard-error-bound display preceding equation (16)]

ambiguities.issue: G₁ is introduced without an explicit quantifier, dimensions, diagonality, or componentwise bounds. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: standard-error-bound display preceding equation (16)]
ambiguities.evidence: The source only prints q₁=(I+G₁)a₁/r₁₁ and ||G₁||₂≤ε_M, prefaced by 'standard error bounds.' [PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: standard-error-bound display preceding equation (16)]
ambiguities.impact: The minimally faithful logical form is existential with a dimension-compatible operator G₁; a formalization must not silently strengthen it by requiring G₁ to be diagonal or componentwise bounded. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: same G₁ display]

ambiguities.issue: The paper explicitly displays a relative-error rule only for addition, yet invokes standard error bounds for the norm and componentwise division used to form r₁₁ and q₁. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: floating-point model after Algorithm 2; PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: k=1 normalization and standard-error-bound displays]
ambiguities.evidence: The displayed model is fl(x+y)=(x+y)(1+δ) for normalized results; no division or norm formula is stated there, while the appendix later asserts the δ₁ and G₁ bounds. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: normalized-range IEEE model; PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: k=1 error bounds]
ambiguities.impact: The δ₁ and G₁ relations should be treated as asserted source facts; their derivation cannot be reconstructed uniquely from the single displayed addition rule. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: k=1 error bounds]

ambiguities.issue: Theorem 1 globally qualifies its conclusions by O(ε_M²), but the G₁ relation and equation (16) are printed with no higher-order remainder. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: Theorem 1 preamble; PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: standard-error-bound display and equation (16)]
ambiguities.evidence: The paper says the computed matrices satisfy (4)-(8) 'to within terms of O(ε_M²),' while equation (16) ends exactly at ε_M||a₁||₂. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: preamble to (4)-(8); PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: equation (16)]
ambiguities.impact: A faithful contract must preserve both facts: equation (16)'s displayed bound has no O term, but its placement in a globally first-order analysis should not be hidden. The paper supplies no O-constant or ε_M threshold for a fully explicit replacement. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: linear approximation; PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: theorem qualification; PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: equation (16)]

ambiguities.issue: Condition (3) is written using R_k⁻¹ through κ₂(R_k), and the paper then says that the condition assures nonsingularity, without specifying an extended condition-number convention for singular R_k. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: κ₂ definition, condition (3), and paragraph after Theorem 1; PDF p. 9, printed p. 307, anchor: nonsingularity consequence]
ambiguities.evidence: κ₂(R_k) is defined as ||R_k||₂||R_k⁻¹||₂ before condition (3), while the later text uses (3) to conclude R is nonsingular and rₖₖ>0. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: κ₂ definition and condition (3); PDF p. 9, printed p. 307, anchor: nonsingularity paragraph]
ambiguities.impact: A formalization must choose whether condition (3) carries invertibility as a well-formedness premise or whether κ₂ is extended by infinity on singular matrices; it cannot silently omit the condition's nonsingularity/positivity role. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: condition (3); PDF p. 9, printed p. 307, anchor: rₖₖ>0 conclusion]

ambiguities.issue: The cited pages use ||·||₂ for vectors and matrices without an explicit local definition of the two norm types. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 300, anchor: algorithm norm notation; PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: κ₂ definition; PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: equation (16)]
ambiguities.evidence: Equation (16) moves from an m×1 matrix residual to a vector residual and applies ||G₁a₁||₂≤||G₁||₂||a₁||₂, which is consistent with Euclidean vector and induced spectral matrix norms. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: exact residual identity and equation (16)]
ambiguities.impact: That standard Euclidean/spectral interpretation is strongly indicated but inherited convention rather than an explicit definition in the selected passage; substituting a different matrix norm would require rechecking the chain. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: equation (16)]

contract_plain_english: In the paper's standing full-column-rank real matrix setting, run Algorithm 2 in the stated IEEE, normalized-range, first-order model and assume Theorem 1's conditioning restriction for every leading block; this restriction is used to ensure the computed r₁₁ is positive. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 300, anchor: opening matrix setting; PDF p. 3, printed p. 301, anchor: Algorithm 2 and floating-point model; PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: condition (3); PDF p. 9, printed p. 307, anchor: nonsingularity paragraph] For the first column, standard error bounds provide a compatible G₁ with q₁=(I+G₁)a₁/r₁₁ and ||G₁||₂≤ε_M. Consequently A₁−Q₁R₁=a₁−q₁r₁₁=−G₁a₁ exactly, and ||A₁−Q₁R₁||₂=||a₁−q₁r₁₁||₂≤||G₁||₂||a₁||₂≤ε_M||a₁||₂. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: standard-error-bound display, exact residual identity, and equation (16)] This is the k=1 case of Theorem 1's perturbation result (4), with c₁(m,1)=1 and the opposite residual sign absorbed into ΔA₁. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 302, anchor: definition (2) and conclusion (4); PDF p. 10, printed p. 308, anchor: equation (16)]
